nodes.summary: An extended nonnegative real $s$ is an admissible planar threshold when $0 \le s \le 2$ and $s$ has the planar threshold property: every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ with Hausdorff dimension $\dim_H E > s$ has a distance set of positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: Admissible planar threshold

nodes.summary: There is an admissible planar threshold, that is, the set of admissible planar thresholds is nonempty.
nodes.title: Admissible planar thresholds exist

nodes.summary: Every subset $E$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfies $\dim_H E \le 2$.
nodes.title: Subsets of the plane have Hausdorff dimension at most two

nodes.summary: For every $d$, the distance set of the empty subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$ is empty.
nodes.title: Distance set of the empty set

nodes.summary: If $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is compact, then the distance set of $E$ is a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Distance sets of compact sets are compact

nodes.summary: If $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is compact, then the distance set of $E$ is a Borel measurable subset of $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Distance sets of compact sets are Borel

nodes.summary: For every point $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the distance set of $\{x\}$ is $\{0\}$.
nodes.title: Distance set of a singleton

nodes.summary: For every set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, the distance set of $E$ is contained in $[0, \infty)$.
nodes.title: Distances are nonnegative

nodes.summary: For a set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, the distance set of $E$ is $\Delta(E) = \{\lvert x - y \rvert : x, y \in E\}$, the set of Euclidean distances between pairs of points of $E$.
nodes.title: Euclidean distance set

nodes.summary: For every integer $d \ge 2$ and every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ whose Hausdorff dimension is strictly greater than $(d+1)/2$, the distance set $\{\|x - y\| : x, y \in E\}$ has positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: Falconer's distance set theorem

nodes.summary: This is the proposition that for every integer $d \ge 2$ and every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ whose Hausdorff dimension is strictly greater than $(d+1)/2$, the distance set $\{\|x - y\| : x, y \in E\}$ has positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: Statement of Falconer's distance set theorem

nodes.summary: For every integer $d \ge 2$ and every $s$ with $0 \le s \le d/2$, there is a compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ of Hausdorff dimension exactly $s$ whose distance set $\{\|x - y\| : x, y \in E\}$ has one-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero.
nodes.title: Falconer's measure-zero distance set examples

nodes.summary: This is the proposition that for every integer $d \ge 2$ and every $s$ with $0 \le s \le d/2$, there is a compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ of Hausdorff dimension exactly $s$ whose distance set $\{\|x - y\| : x, y \in E\}$ has one-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero.
nodes.title: Statement of Falconer's measure-zero distance set examples

nodes.summary: Every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ whose Hausdorff dimension is strictly greater than $5/4$ has a distance set $\{\|x - y\| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: Guth–Iosevich–Ou–Wang planar distance set theorem

nodes.summary: This is the proposition that $5/4$ has the planar threshold property: every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ whose Hausdorff dimension is strictly greater than $5/4$ has a distance set $\{\|x - y\| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: Statement of the Guth–Iosevich–Ou–Wang planar distance set theorem

nodes.summary: The planar distance threshold is the least admissible planar threshold: it is itself an admissible planar threshold, and it is at most every admissible planar threshold.
nodes.title: The planar distance threshold is attained

nodes.summary: Let $t \in [0, \infty]$. If $E$ is a compact subset of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose Hausdorff dimension $\dim_H E$ satisfies $t \le \dim_H E$ and whose distance set has Lebesgue measure zero, then $t$ is at most the planar distance threshold.
nodes.title: Zero-measure distance sets give lower bounds for the planar distance threshold

nodes.summary: The planar distance threshold, the infimum of all $s \in [0, 2]$ such that every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of Hausdorff dimension strictly greater than $s$ has a distance set $\{\|x - y\| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure, is at least $1$.
nodes.title: Falconer's lower bound for the planar distance threshold

nodes.summary: This is the proposition that the planar distance threshold, the infimum of all $s \in [0, 2]$ such that every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of Hausdorff dimension strictly greater than $s$ has a distance set $\{\|x - y\| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure, is at least $1$.
nodes.title: Statement of the lower bound $1$ for the planar distance threshold

nodes.summary: For every real number $s \ge 0$, $s$ is an admissible planar threshold (as an element of $[0, \infty]$) if and only if $s \in [0, 2]$ and $s$ has the planar threshold property.
nodes.title: Real form of admissible planar thresholds

nodes.summary: The planar distance threshold is an admissible planar threshold: it lies in $[0, 2]$ and has the planar threshold property.
nodes.title: The planar distance threshold is admissible

nodes.summary: For every $s \in [0, \infty]$ that is an admissible planar threshold, the planar distance threshold is at most $s$.
nodes.title: Admissible thresholds bound the planar distance threshold

nodes.summary: Thresholds up to two with the planar threshold property bound the planar distance threshold. For every $s \in [0, \infty]$ with $s \le 2$ that has the planar threshold property, the planar distance threshold is at most $s$.
nodes.title: Thresholds up to two with the planar threshold property bound the planar distance threshold

nodes.summary: The planar distance threshold is at most $2$.
nodes.title: The planar distance threshold is at most two

nodes.summary: The planar distance threshold, an element of $[0, \infty]$, is not $\infty$.
nodes.title: The planar distance threshold is finite

nodes.summary: Let $\tau \in [0, \infty]$ be the planar distance threshold and let $\tau_{\mathbb{R}}$ be its value as a real number (with the convention that $\infty$ goes to $0$). Viewing $\tau_{\mathbb{R}}$ again as an element of $[0, \infty]$ gives back $\tau$.
nodes.title: Real round trip of the planar distance threshold

nodes.summary: The value of the planar distance threshold as a real number (with the convention that $\infty$ goes to $0$) equals the infimum in $\mathbb{R}$ of the set of real numbers $r \in [0, 2]$ that, as elements of $[0, \infty]$, have the planar threshold property.
nodes.title: The planar distance threshold as a real infimum

nodes.summary: The planar distance threshold is the infimum, taken in $[0, \infty]$, of the admissible planar thresholds, that is, of all $s \in [0, 2]$ such that every compact subset $E$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with Hausdorff dimension greater than $s$ has a distance set of positive Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: Planar distance threshold

nodes.summary: Let $s \le t$ be elements of $[0, \infty]$. If $s$ has the planar threshold property, that is, every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ with Hausdorff dimension $\dim_H E > s$ has a distance set of positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure, then $t$ has the planar threshold property.
nodes.title: The planar threshold property is upward closed

nodes.summary: Let $s_0 \in [0, \infty]$ be the planar distance threshold, the infimum of the admissible planar thresholds. Every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ with Hausdorff dimension $\dim_H E > s_0$ has a distance set of positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: The planar distance threshold is itself a threshold

nodes.summary: An element $s \in [0, \infty]$ has the planar threshold property when every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ with Hausdorff dimension $\dim_H E > s$ has a distance set $\{|x - y| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: Planar Falconer threshold property

nodes.summary: The set of real numbers $r \in [0, 2]$ such that $r$, viewed as an element of $[0, \infty]$, has the planar threshold property equals the image of the set of admissible planar thresholds under the map $[0, \infty] \to \mathbb{R}$ that is the identity on finite values and sends $\infty$ to $0$.
nodes.title: Real form of the admissible threshold family

nodes.summary: The planar distance threshold is at least $0$.
nodes.title: Trivial lower bound for the planar distance threshold

nodes.summary: The number $2$ is an admissible planar threshold: $2 \in [0, 2]$, and every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ with Hausdorff dimension $\dim_H E > 2$ has a distance set of positive Lebesgue measure. This holds vacuously, since no subset of the plane has Hausdorff dimension greater than $2$.
nodes.title: Two is an admissible planar threshold

nodes.summary: The planar distance threshold, the infimum of all $s \in [0, 2]$ such that every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of Hausdorff dimension strictly greater than $s$ has a distance set $\{\|x - y\| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure, is at most $3/2$.
nodes.title: Falconer's upper bound for the planar distance threshold

nodes.summary: This is the proposition that the planar distance threshold, the infimum of all $s \in [0, 2]$ such that every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of Hausdorff dimension strictly greater than $s$ has a distance set $\{\|x - y\| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure, is at most $3/2$.
nodes.title: Statement of the upper bound $3/2$ for the planar distance threshold

nodes.summary: The planar Falconer distance threshold, the infimum of the $s \in [0, 2]$ such that every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ with Hausdorff dimension greater than $s$ has a distance set $\{|x - y| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive Lebesgue measure, is at most $5/4$.
nodes.title: Guth–Iosevich–Ou–Wang upper bound for the planar Falconer threshold

nodes.summary: The proposition that the planar Falconer distance threshold is at most $5/4$. Here the planar Falconer distance threshold is the infimum of the $s \in [0, 2]$ such that every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ with Hausdorff dimension greater than $s$ has a distance set $\{|x - y| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: The Guth–Iosevich–Ou–Wang bound, as a proposition

nodes.summary: The planar Falconer distance threshold, the infimum of the $s \in [0, 2]$ such that every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ with Hausdorff dimension greater than $s$ has a distance set $\{|x - y| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive Lebesgue measure, is at most $4/3$.
nodes.title: Wolff's upper bound for the planar Falconer threshold

nodes.summary: The proposition that the planar Falconer distance threshold is at most $4/3$. Here the planar Falconer distance threshold is the infimum of the $s \in [0, 2]$ such that every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ with Hausdorff dimension greater than $s$ has a distance set $\{|x - y| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: The Wolff bound, as a proposition

nodes.summary: Every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ with Hausdorff dimension greater than $4/3$ has a distance set $\{|x - y| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: Wolff's planar distance set theorem

nodes.summary: The proposition that every compact set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ with Hausdorff dimension greater than $4/3$ has a distance set $\{|x - y| : x, y \in E\}$ of positive Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: Wolff's planar distance set condition, as a proposition

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
